title: Probabilistic Models of Cognition (2nd edition)
authors: The ProbMods Contributors (Daphna Buchsbaum, Joshua Hartshorne, Robert Hawkins, Timothy J. O'Donnell, Michael Henry Tessler, and others named on the site)
institution: probmods.org (open-source book project; source on GitHub, probmods/probmods2)
description: Web book on probabilistic generative models of cognition written around runnable WebPPL programs: generative models, conditioning, dependence, social cognition, Bayesian data analysis, inference algorithms, process models, learning as conditional inference, hierarchical models, Occam's razor, mixture models and more. Cited by the site as N. D. Goodman, J. B. Tenenbaum and The ProbMods Contributors (2016), Probabilistic Models of Cognition (2nd ed.).
rightsNotes: No licence is stated anywhere inspected on 2026-10-30: the site index says only 'This book is an open source project. We welcome content contributions'; the probmods/probmods2 repository shows no LICENSE file and its README contains no licence sentence. Under Corniversity's rules an unknown licence means reference-only: the book is read on its own site, cited by chapter URL and heading, never imported, embedded or sent to an external model.

The site serves over plain HTTP. On 2026-10-30 the HTTPS endpoint presented a certificate for *.github.io that does not cover probmods.org, so verification used http://probmods.org/ (HTTP 200, Server: GitHub.com, Last-Modified 2023-06-05) and the chapter headings were cross-checked against the GitHub source.
The first edition (Goodman & Tenenbaum, Church-based) remains at https://v1.probmods.org/ with a different chapter list; it is not used here.

limitations: Licence unknown: reference-only. The tutor may discuss and cite the chapters; the worker must not ingest them.
Runnable WebPPL code boxes require JavaScript in the learner's own browser on the book's site; Corniversity labs are separate implementations and do not depend on WebPPL.
HTTPS is not correctly served for the custom domain (certificate mismatch on 2026-10-30); links use http://.

Chapters 'Function learning', 'Learning with a language of thought', 'Non-parametric models', 'Agents as programs' and 'Sequential decisions' were listed on the index but not opened; no locators for them.
The chapter_num front matter is non-sequential in the source (e.g. Bayesian data analysis is 6.5); Corniversity orders chapters by its own syllabus, not the book's numbering.
